opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is permitted for this employee. Recommend admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 (Miguel Benson) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; without advanced training, max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The two team notes conflict on employment type: HR lists E006 as full-time Engineer, while Security lists E006 as a contractor with basic security training. As Approver, I side with the Security database record. Under policy, contractors never receive admin; without advanced training, the maximum level for a contractor is read. The requested admin exceeds read, so I grant the maximum allowed: read.

Contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
